subject: Post-demo: Sandbox & SDK bootstrap checklist / tech deep-dive
messages:
From: Sam Li <sam.li@brightarc.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: SDK/bootstrap needs + security checklist

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team at BrightArc liked the latency numbers and the routing/fallback story. A few follow-ups from our side so we can spin up a local sandbox and validate integrations: 

- SDKs: we want Python + TypeScript quickstarts (dev and prod examples) and the minimal auth flow you recommend for early testing.
- Auth: two options in play: API key for sandbox, and OIDC integration for our pre-prod. Do you have guidance (and sample configs) for both?
- Routing/model choices: we'd like a recommended starter configuration for a 2-model flow (short prompt & long-context).
- Structured output / tool calling: examples that show tool-calling with a typed JSON schema would be ideal.
- Embeddings / rerankers: any simple reranker example using embeddings and a BM25-like fallback?

Attached are our security questionnaire highlights (we'll need SOC 2 artifacts and an outline of network isolation options). We also have a handful of constraints: on-prem evaluation for compliance, and strict egress rules for token telemetry.

Can you send a prioritized checklist + a proposed 60-minute deep-dive slot with an infra engineer?

Thanks — Sam
Sam Li
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightArc
attachments: BrightArc-security-questions.pdf

From: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>

Sam — great to hear the demo resonated. I've sketched a short, prioritized checklist below to get your engineers into a local sandbox quickly and then into a constrained pre-prod (OIDC + VPC). Attaching a small markdown quickstart for Python and a repo list. Links and next steps at the bottom.

Priority 1 — Local dev sandbox (30–60 min):
- Pull sample-app quickstart repo (Python + TS) and run docker-compose example (no GPU, CPU inference).
- Create a sandbox API key (short TTL) and set REDWOOD_API_KEY locally.
- Run the sample that demonstrates: text generation, streaming, and simple structured output.

Priority 2 — Auth + pre-prod (1–2 days):
- OIDC: we'll provide an example config for AWS Cognito / Okta and a small guide for OIDC client credentials flow (token exchange + caching).
- Network isolation: for Private deployments we provide customer-managed VPC options; we'll share a network diagram and minimal firewall rules.

Priority 3 — Routing & model config (tune after smoke tests):
- Starter routing: short-context model for chat-like interactions, long-context model for document summarization; automatic fallback to a quantized variant during capacity constraints.
- Batching and KV-cache settings for interactive latency — default suggestions included in quickstart.

Priority 4 — Embeddings & rerankers:
- Example pipeline: embed -> store (FAISS) -> candidate set -> rerank with lightweight cross-encoder. Sample notebooks included in repo list.

Priority 5 — Tool-calling/structured output:
- Example shows schema-first JSON output with field validation and an example tool (calendar create) using function-call style payloads.

Action items / attachments:
- Attached: redwood-sdk-python-quickstart.md (walkthrough), redwood-sampleapps-repo-list.txt (repo links).
- Shared links: quickstarts GitHub, sandbox drive for config.
- I'll loop Marissa (solutions eng) and Ben (platform) on a proposed deep-dive time; please confirm your timezone preference.

Proposed times: Wed 3/7 09:00–10:00 PT or Thu 3/8 13:00–14:00 PT

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Sam — adding a few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so the discussion can hit the ground running: 

- Python quickstart: will include a minimal local server showing both streaming and structured output via a /generate endpoint. We instrument a sample JSON Schema validation step and a small test harness (pytest) for structured responses.
- TypeScript example: shows both SDK client usage and a Next.js sample that streams tokens to the browser.
- OIDC nuances: for our OIDC guide, we'll include example claims mapping and a short-lived client-credentials sample that exchanges to an access token + caching TTL recommendations.
- Embeddings: we'll provide a small notebook that computes embeddings with the hosted model, stores vectors in an open-source vector DB, and then demonstrates cosine retrieval + a rerank step.
- On-prem notes: for your compliance constraints we can provide a minimum-config on-prem package (air-gapped install) and an audit-log extractor for SOC 2 evidence.

I'll bring the reranker notebook and a small demo script to the deep-dive. If you can share a representative query set beforehand, we'll tailor the reranker example to your domain.

—Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
